topics.label: Lecture introduction and overview
topics.groupedBecause: This opening section welcomes students and outlines the lecture's focus on the initiation and resolution of inflammation.

topics.label: Innate immune recognition of infection and damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the innate immune system identifies danger by detecting pathogen- and damage-associated molecular patterns through pattern recognition receptor signaling.

topics.label: Execution and systemic effects of acute inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the cellular and vascular mechanisms through which sentinel cells coordinate leukocyte recruitment, fluid drainage, and potential systemic inflammatory consequences.

topics.label: Inflammatory resolution, tissue repair, and chronic inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the mechanisms required to terminate acute inflammation, rebuild damaged tissues, and manage chronic inflammatory states.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and next steps
topics.groupedBecause: This closing remark concludes the presentation and introduces the topic of the following lecture.
